summary: Final results are published, with Netanyahu's camp ahead but short of a majority; President Herzog receives the official results on Nov 4, his faction consultations will be broadcast live, and the new Knesset is sworn in on Nov 10. Eisenkot has set four conditions for partners and says he will form only a Zionist government, and a source close to him tells Ynet he is courting Shas and UTJ, with Liberman the main obstacle. Maariv reports the opposition has agreed its first move will be to replace Knesset Speaker Amir Ohana, while the Joint List's Tibi says his party won't join a government. Netanyahu is holding his partners together, and Ynet reports Likud is working to peel lawmakers away from the opposition's speaker bid.

phase.now: Final results published by the Central Elections Committee; no change between the blocs
phase.next: Official results go to President Herzog on Nov 4; Haaretz reports his consultations with the factions will be broadcast live, and the new Knesset is sworn in on Nov 10.

scenarios.name: Netanyahu's Right-Religious Bloc
scenarios.note: His existing partners, whom he told they are staying together. Without a majority, Netanyahu needs defectors or a new partner from the other side.

blockers.text: Liberman urged Likud MKs to revolt against Netanyahu rather than join him.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Arab Parties
scenarios.note: Championed by Yair Golan, who met Lapid and then Abbas on Oct 29; the Times of Israel says he is the only Jewish-led bloc leader openly backing a coalition with Ra'am. Without Yisrael Beiteinu it falls short, and analysts told JTA the public is not ready for it. Channel 12 reports Abbas himself privately called an Eisenkot minority government with outside Arab support weak or impossible. AFP reports Eisenkot has not decided whether to seek a coalition relying on Arab parties, and the Joint List's Jabareen says he would back him from outside.

blockers.text: Liberman ruled out Ra'am, the Joint List and any minority government.
Eisenkot pledged a 'Zionist government' and has not backed the idea.
Ben-Gvir urged the Shin Bet to arrest Arab party leaders if there are legal grounds over alleged Qatari funding.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Ra'am Only
scenarios.note: The 2021 Bennett–Lapid model. Abbas says both camps have contacted him, but this falls short of 61 even before Liberman's veto.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Shas And UTJ
scenarios.note: No Arab parties needed, but the Haredi draft splits it. A source close to Eisenkot tells Ynet he is trying to bring Shas and UTJ into a government he leads, naming Liberman as the main obstacle. A senior UTJ official told Ynet the party would offer Eisenkot the premiership for draft exemptions, which clashes with his national-service condition; Shas is reported to be out.

blockers.text: Haredi sources tell the Jerusalem Post that Deri won't join an opposition-led government without Likud.
Shas and UTJ say they won't join any government unless yeshiva students' exemptions are written into law.
Liberman told party members on Oct 29 that his pledge not to sit with the Haredi parties stands.
Eisenkot's core promise is national service for all.

scenarios.name: National Unity Government
scenarios.note: The Jerusalem Post reports Netanyahu-linked sources are promoting it, possibly with a rotating premiership and without Shas and UTJ, but Ynet reports Netanyahu has not discussed it with his partners or Likud associates. Channel 12 reports Liberman wants Eisenkot to join Netanyahu, though not under his own banner. Who would lead it is the sticking point.

blockers.text: Eisenkot rules out serving under Netanyahu, including in a rotation.
Channel 12 reports Liberman still refuses to join a Netanyahu-led government, even as he urges Eisenkot to.
Ben-Gvir warned Netanyahu against a unity government with Eisenkot.

scenarios.name: Netanyahu Plus Bennett's Together
scenarios.note: Ideologically the closest fit, but Bennett and Lapid campaigned on replacing Netanyahu.

blockers.text: Bennett declared on election night that Netanyahu has lost.

מחל.stance: Netanyahu posted on Oct 30 that forming a government with the Arab-led parties is forbidden; Likud says the election was stolen.
red_lines: No government that depends on Arab parties

דרך.stance: After meeting Lapid on Oct 31, Eisenkot said any MK accepting his four principles could be a partner, and vowed to use a Knesset majority for a state inquiry, national service and repealing judicial-overhaul laws.
red_lines: Partners must accept his four principles

רק.stance: Lapid says Netanyahu has no way to form a government on these results, but forming an alternative will be complicated and is not guaranteed.

אמת.stance: Golan met Lapid and then Abbas on Oct 29 in his push to oust Netanyahu, and is the only Jewish-led opposition leader openly backing a coalition with Ra'am.

ל.stance: In a Facebook post on Oct 30, Liberman again ruled out a coalition with the Arab parties, saying he won't sit with supporters of terrorism; he also still won't sit with Netanyahu or the Haredi parties.

שס.stance: Unnamed Haredi sources say Deri has ruled out an opposition-led government without Likud and would join a unity government only alongside Likud.

ג.stance: Rabbi Dov Landau reportedly urged Degel HaTorah MKs to consider joining an opposition coalition, and unnamed UTJ sources voice cautious optimism about a draft compromise.

ב.stance: Ben-Gvir held a long meeting with Netanyahu on Oct 29 on preserving a right-wing government, his party says; he rejects unity with Eisenkot.

ט.stance: Smotrich met Netanyahu in person on Oct 29, Ynet reports, and says the Arab party heads should be questioned by the Shin Bet over alleged foreign funding.

עם.stance: Abbas denies any link to the alleged foreign interference, pledges full cooperation with investigators and accuses Netanyahu of inciting against Arab citizens; he has said he'd join a government that tackles crime and discrimination.

ודם.stance: Joint List MK Ahmad Tibi said on Oct 31 the party will not be part of the government, though Jabareen has offered Eisenkot outside support; KAN reports its leaders felt snubbed by the opposition's talks.

timeline.text: Has agreed that its first move will be to replace Knesset Speaker Amir Ohana, Maariv reports, citing local news reports.

Plans to open coalition consultations with the Knesset factions next week and broadcast them live, dpa reports, citing Haaretz.
Sets four conditions for coalition partners, including national service for all and treating Hamas as a terror group, and says he aims for a broad Zionist government.
Accuses Likud's Yoav Kisch, Almog Cohen and Yaakov Bardugo of phoning Yashar! members to try to win them over.
Meet and say in a joint statement that they discussed the results and coordinated next steps.
Maariv reports unnamed senior opposition figures are weighing a direct election for prime minister without dissolving the Knesset.
Writes on Facebook that he will not sit with supporters of terrorism, again ruling out a coalition with the Arab parties.
Posts on X that it is forbidden to form a government relying on the Arab-led parties, Al Jazeera reports.
Says Netanyahu cannot form a government on these results, while warning an alternative coalition is complicated and not guaranteed.
Degel HaTorah's senior rabbi reportedly urged its MKs to consider joining an opposition coalition, saying they belong to no one's bloc.
Unnamed Haredi sources say he has ruled out joining an opposition-led government without Likud.
Publishes the final election results and says the new Knesset will be sworn in on Nov. 10.
Holds a lengthy meeting with Netanyahu on preserving a right-wing government, according to his party.
Unnamed sources tell Ynet the Haredi parties would negotiate joining an Eisenkot government if a draft-exemption law is passed.
Tells party members his pledges not to sit with the Haredi or Arab parties remain in place.
Meets Smotrich in person after calling him and Ben-Gvir the night before; Ynet says talks with the Haredi parties are expected next.
The UTJ chairman denies any feelers, talks or contacts with Eisenkot, after Channel 12 reported UTJ officials were weighing outside support for an Eisenkot minority government.
Channel 12 reports he told party members that an Eisenkot minority government relying on outside Arab support would be weak or impossible.
Acting director Dean Livne tells Channel 12 he sees no likelihood the interference allegations will change the results, with individual votes voided only on direct proof.
Meets Ra'am chairman Mansour Abbas as part of his efforts to form a government without Netanyahu.
Meets Bennett at his Ra'anana home; their joint statement says they discussed forming a good government as quickly as possible.
After briefings from the elections committee and the Shin Bet chief, says there is no reason to challenge the results or delay the Knesset's swearing-in.
Accuses Netanyahu of a coordinated bid to delegitimize the results, vows the Knesset will be sworn in on schedule, and says conscription and Oct. 7 inquiry bills are being prepared.
A senior unnamed UTJ official tells Ynet the party intends to offer Eisenkot the premiership if draft-exemption legislation is advanced.
With the double-envelope count almost done, a seat moves from the Joint List to Ra'am, with no change between the blocs.
Says that, given the interference allegations, no Zionist party can partner with Ra'am or the Joint List.
